title: Choosing authentication for high-risk administrators — question explanation
learningObjective: Select phishing-resistant authentication for high-risk contexts and address fallback risks
format: 16:9 educational motion-graphics video; narration; separate captions; no autoplay with sound
visualStyle: Deep navy and charcoal; restrained cyan/electric-blue highlights; limited purple accents; clean typography; purposeful, low-motion transitions; accessible contrast.

scenes.name: Scenario setup
scenes.visual: An organization is redesigning authentication for privileged administrators. Options include password plus SMS OTP, push approval, or phishing-resistant public-key authentication, but legacy recovery remains weak.
scenes.direction: Show a fictional simulated setting. Use generic UI and no actual organization, brand, user identity, credential, real URL or live account.

scenes.name: Learning objective and risk cue
scenes.visual: Select phishing-resistant authentication for high-risk contexts and address fallback risks
scenes.direction: Highlight only observable cues and explain the decision context without implying certainty beyond the scenario.

scenes.name: Recommended response
scenes.visual: Option C: Adopt phishing-resistant authentication such as FIDO/WebAuthn for privileged access and harden enrollment, recovery and fallback paths. Strong primary authentication must be supported by secure lifecycle and recovery processes.
scenes.direction: Animate the recommended defensive choice as a clear decision path. Display the action verb and trusted channel/control.

scenes.name: Why the other options fail
scenes.visual: Option A: Unbounded prompts can enable fatigue attacks and do not provide strong phishing resistance. Option B: SMS OTP adds a factor but is not phishing-resistant and weak recovery can undermine the primary control. Option D: A longer password alone does not provide the assurance or phishing resistance required for privileged access.
scenes.direction: Show each unsafe alternative separately with a complete, concise reason. Do not depict operational exploitation, malicious code or credential capture.

scenes.name: Defensive takeaway
scenes.visual: Use standards-aligned phishing-resistant authenticators where feasible, tightly control fallback, bind credentials to legitimate verifiers and monitor recovery events. Choose phishing-resistant authenticators for high-risk access and secure the entire account lifecycle, including recovery.
scenes.direction: Close with one readable takeaway and the next safe action. Keep the final frame long enough for comprehension.

narration: Scenario: An organization is redesigning authentication for privileged administrators. Options include password plus SMS OTP, push approval, or phishing-resistant public-key authentication, but legacy recovery remains weak. Safest response: Option C: Adopt phishing-resistant authentication such as FIDO/WebAuthn for privileged access and harden enrollment, recovery and fallback paths. Strong primary authentication must be supported by secure lifecycle and recovery processes. Option A is unsafe because Unbounded prompts can enable fatigue attacks and do not provide strong phishing resistance. Option B is unsafe because SMS OTP adds a factor but is not phishing-resistant and weak recovery can undermine the primary control. Option D is unsafe because A longer password alone does not provide the assurance or phishing resistance required for privileged access. In practice: Use standards-aligned phishing-resistant authenticators where feasible, tightly control fallback, bind credentials to legitimate verifiers and monitor recovery events. Key takeaway: Choose phishing-resistant authenticators for high-risk access and secure the entire account lifecycle, including recovery.
